Sandy Cadillac Escalade-V Gets a Carbon Suit Overseas
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign
Can the fifth-generation Cadillac Escalade still make headlines even though it is not exactly new anymore? Well, it certainly can. After all, its predecessor still get a touch of the limelight every now and then.
Assembly kicked off at the Arlington facility in Texas in 2020, and four years later, the full-size premium SUV was given a mid-cycle refresh, receiving a new front fascia, new colors, wheels, and a few enhancements on the inside, including the curved 55-inch display. Despite looking similar to the IQ , it does not share its underpinnings, as it is based on the same platform as the Chevy Suburban, Tahoe, and GMC’s Yukon, whereas the zero-emission shares its nuts and bolts with the Hummer EV.
But you already knew that, so we’d better get back on track and put the spotlight on the example pictured in the gallery. This Cadillac Escalade-V came directly from Larte Design’s portfolio. The tuner has given it that sandy look mentioned in the title, stating that this machine is “in a color that nobody else is parking next to you,” and that is correct, especially when you combine it with their carbon fiber bits and pieces.
Part of the Esthete body kit, the extras has been made from carbon fiber, and feature a dry carbon look on the SUV in question. One does not need to be a connoisseur of this model to tell that the vented hood has come from the aftermarket world. The same goes for the grille surround, and the new double-layer splitter that extends on the sides of the OEM bumper.
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign It seems that the side skirts on this Cadillac Escalade-V have also come from Larte Design’s portfolio, and so has the rear diffuser with its multi-fin design, and cutouts for the quad exhaust tips. There is also a roof-mounted wing on deck, as well as wheel arch attachments. The pictured SUV rides on new wheels that appear to have come from Vossen’s portfolio, and they spin around a set of red brake calipers.
This is one Cadillac Escalade-V that easily stands out from the crowd due to its satin sand look and dry carbon components, as well as the new alloys, and several black details, but the question is whether it rocks this look like champ or not. So, where do you stand on that?
Before inviting you to scroll down and leave your impression on this tuned ride, we will remind you that it features a supercharged 6.2-liter V8 engine breathing air from behind that imposing grille. The Escalade-V has 682 hp (691 ps/508 kW ) and 653 lb-ft (885 Nm) of torque on tap, taking a manufacturer-estimated 4.4 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph). So, what’s your take on the pictured Caddy? Is it a yay or a nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by LARTE DESIGN | BODY KITS | WHEELS | AUTO DESIGN (@lartedesign)
